name: Naha
registryBasis: Naha City publishes local cadastral survey results, and a public CC BY 2026 converted MOJ cadastral shapefile for Naha (municipality code 47201) was retrieved anonymously and inspected schema-first. Full static footprint contains 136,440 polygons; bounded samples around the official city-hall reference confirm Naha binding. The WUP locator is outside Naha and the dataset extent, with no feature at that exact point; this does not negate the city-bound source.
pointBasis: UN WUP 2025 population-weighted settlement centroid; this is not a municipal boundary or a parcel-coverage claim.
technicalBlocker: Existing repository runtime adapters do not support this static Shapefile archive. The full-snapshot composite identifier scan found 136,412 unique nonmissing composite keys across 136,440 features, with 28 duplicate extra rows in 19 key groups and 0 missing keys; duplicate identity resolution remains open. The 257-feature bounded GEOS audit found 2 invalid polygons and 13 positive-area overlap/containment pairs (12 above 0.01 m²; maximum 39.24210 m²). Arbitrary footprint and runtime source binding have not been qualified; no adapter was implemented or enabled.
scopeLimits: A public CC BY 2026 Naha converted MOJ snapshot contains 136,440 native EPSG:6683 polygons bound to municipality code 47201. The 13-window city-hall-centered sample returned 257 records; full composite-key scan and GEOS summary are in the recorded Naha full-257 review. The full snapshot has 28 repeated composite-key rows and 0 missing keys; 257 bounded records had distinct nonmissing keys. GEOS on the 257 bounded union found 2 invalid polygons and 13 overlap/containment pairs, so the source needs additional identity and geometry review before any runtime use.
remainingUncertainty: The unchanged WUP point [26.2485177206029,127.737901051124] lies outside Naha (official 2026 boundary code 47208 Urasoe) and outside this archive footprint; this is scope information, not a source eligibility blocker. Full source geometry and identity defects/duplicate rows may be non-random; no arbitrary bbox runtime lookup/footprint semantics, exact-ID retrieval or authoritative response binding have been qualified.
